files.notes/operations.md:
# Operations

Keep the last accepted artifact available until its replacement is accepted. Keep preview links and reviews tied to their actual artifact revision: rebuilding a preview does not transfer the previous review to the replacement. Do not reconstruct the accepted artifact from a newer revision and describe it as the reviewed artifact. A failed preview alone does not establish a failed production deployment.

For REST-101, the restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the disposable test volume; otherwise quota estimates are wrong. Ask the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. These constraints also apply to future exercises after allocation or a successful restore. They come from the September 22 uncommitted operator note and remain useful operational context.

Production on-call ownership is unassigned in the supplied records. The escalation contact is an open staffing question; Mira's ownership of decisions does not automatically make her the escalation contact. Receipt storage has not been selected.

See [working state](status.md) for REST-101, the independent CAL-102 blocker and next actions, and [publication notes](release.md) for current policy.

Sources: [preview review](../evidence/03-review.txt), [operator work list](../evidence/04-work.txt), [demonstration](../evidence/05-demo.txt), [operator constraint](../scratch/operator.txt).
files.notes/release.md:
# Publication notes

Owner Mira approved manual publication for the pilot with optional CI (DEC-101, September 8), so the operator reviews every artifact. The approved publication command is `wrangler pages deploy dist`.

Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred proposals. The September 1 contributor design proposed publishing on every main-branch push after mandatory CI to reduce repetitive operator work and tie artifacts to source revisions. Revisit these proposals if release frequency makes setup worthwhile; a newer proposal date does not constitute approval.

The September 20 demonstration note says Git integration might have been enabled, but its screenshot is missing and no owner decision supersedes DEC-101. Actual settings must be confirmed before a real release. Possible implementation is not owner approval, and the demonstration does not establish the deployed revision or publication path.

The September 21 local build produced an artifact. A staging-only preview receipt names `sample-17`; neither establishes a production rollout, production revision or runtime timeout. No production receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied. Receipt storage remains undecided.

Follow the [artifact acceptance rules](operations.md) when reviewing replacements. The [content boundary](boundaries.md) remains in force regardless of publication method. See [working state](status.md) for follow-up work; no live verification or deployment has been performed for this documentation update.

Sources: [design](../evidence/01-design.txt), [DEC-101](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [demonstration](../evidence/05-demo.txt), [local build](../evidence/06-build.txt).
files.notes/status.md:
# Working state

Reconciled from supplied evidence through September 22, 2026. No live environment access is supplied.

The checked-in [service configuration](../config/service.yaml) sets `timeout_seconds: 60`, consistent with the September 21 local build observation. The earlier 30-second value was a September 1 design proposal intended to limit operator time spent on failed builds; it is not the current checked-in value. The production timeout remains unknown.

A local build produced an artifact, and a staging-only preview receipt names revision `sample-17`. This does not establish production deployment, revision, publication path or runtime settings. No production receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied. The possible Git integration reported in the demonstration remains unconfirmed and does not supersede [DEC-101](release.md).

| Open item | Supported state | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REST-101 | Blocked: no disposable restore volume allocated. | Operator asks the storage maintainer before reserving a volume, requests the volume, then runs and records the restore exercise. Preserve the [fixture and sparse-file constraints](operations.md). |
| CAL-102 | Independently blocked: calibration sample lacks a leading-zero sensor identifier. | Ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample. |
| Release settings and production evidence | Git integration may have been enabled; actual settings and production state are unverified. | Confirm settings before a real release and obtain production evidence to establish the deployed revision, publication path and runtime timeout. |
| Receipt storage | Not selected. | Select a storage location; no responsible person is identified in the supplied records. |
| Operational staffing | No production on-call owner or escalation contact assigned. | Resolve staffing explicitly; do not assume Mira is the escalation contact. |

Writing a procedure does not resolve REST-101 or CAL-102. No supplied evidence closes either blocker. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred pending a future decision; reconsider when release frequency warrants their setup.

Sources: [design](../evidence/01-design.txt), [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [work list](../evidence/04-work.txt), [demonstration](../evidence/05-demo.txt), [build observation](../evidence/06-build.txt), [operator note](../scratch/operator.txt). See also [content boundaries](boundaries.md) and [operations](operations.md).

# Operations

Keep the last accepted artifact available until its replacement is accepted. Keep preview links and reviews tied to their actual artifact revision: rebuilding a preview does not transfer the previous review to the replacement. Do not reconstruct the accepted artifact from a newer revision and describe it as the reviewed artifact. A failed preview alone does not establish a failed production deployment.

For REST-101, the restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the disposable test volume; otherwise quota estimates are wrong. Ask the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. These constraints also apply to future exercises after allocation or a successful restore. They come from the September 22 uncommitted operator note and remain useful operational context.

REST-101 closed on September 25: the disposable volume was allocated with its sparse-file flag preserved, and the synthetic restore exercise passed, receipt `restore-25`. This result closes only REST-101; it does not remove the constraints above or resolve CAL-102.

# Operator notes

## Artifact review and retention

Keep preview links and reviews tied to their actual artifact revision. Rebuilding a preview does not transfer prior review to the replacement. A failed preview alone does not establish a failed production deployment. Keep the last accepted artifact available until its replacement is accepted; do not rebuild it from a newer revision and call it the reviewed artifact.

Source: [September 13 preview review](../evidence/03-review.txt).

## Restore work and persistent constraints

**REST-101 is closed:** the [September 25 operator update](../evidence/07-update.txt) reports that the disposable volume was allocated with its sparse-file flag preserved and the synthetic restore exercise passed that day, receipt `restore-25`. This resolves the allocation blocker in the [September 15 work list](../evidence/04-work.txt) and closes only REST-101.

For future exercises, the operator must ask the storage maintainer before reserving a test volume, request allocation, then run and record the restore exercise. The restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`; quote this path in shell commands. Preserve its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume or quota estimates will be wrong. These constraints remain applicable after allocation or a successful restore. Source: [September 22 uncommitted operator note](../scratch/operator.txt), preserved here for continuity without removing the original.

## Blocked work

- **CAL-102:** the calibration sample still lacks a leading-zero sensor identifier. Ask the test maintainer for an approved synthetic sample. This blocker is separate from REST-101 and is not resolved by writing a procedure or by the restore passing. Sources: [September 15 work list](../evidence/04-work.txt) and [September 25 update](../evidence/07-update.txt).

## Staffing

No production on-call owner is assigned in the supplied records. Assigning an escalation contact remains an open staffing question; Mira is not automatically that contact. Source: [operator work list](../evidence/04-work.txt).

# Operations and design history

## Design history

The September 1, 2026 contributor design proposed automatic publication on each
main-branch push after mandatory CI to reduce repetitive operator work and tie
artifacts to source revisions. Its proposed 30-second timeout aimed to keep
failed builds from occupying an operator. These were suggestions, not owner
approval or deployment evidence ([design note](../evidence/01-design.txt)).

Mira's September 8 DEC-101 chose manual publication with optional CI for operator
review of every artifact and deferred automation to reduce pilot setup. Release
frequency may justify revisiting setup costs. The canonical approved procedure
is in [release](release.md); the current configured timeout and production
unknowns are in [status](status.md).

## Artifact review

Keep preview links with their artifact revision. Rebuilding a preview does not
transfer the previous review to its replacement. Keep the previous accepted
artifact available until its replacement is accepted; do not reconstruct it
from a newer revision and call that the reviewed artifact. A failed preview
alone does not establish a failed production deployment.

Source: [September 13 reviewer note](../evidence/03-review.txt).

## Restore exercise constraints

The restore fixture is `./data files/pilot.db`. Preserve its sparse-file flag
when allocating the test volume, or quota estimates will be wrong. Ask the
storage maintainer before reserving the volume. These constraints apply to
future exercises even after allocation or a successful restore.

Source: [uncommitted September 22 operator note](../scratch/operator.txt), retained
in place. See [completed REST-101 exercise](status.md#completed-work).

# Release procedure

Owner Mira approved **DEC-101** on September 8, 2026: publish manually for the
pilot, with optional CI, so the operator reviews every artifact. The publication
command is:

```sh
wrangler pages deploy dist
```

Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI remain deferred proposals. Revisit
them if release frequency makes setup worthwhile; a later proposal date is
not approval. See [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt) and
[design rationale](operations.md#design-history).

Before a real release:

1. Confirm actual publication settings. The September 20 contributor demo says
   Git integration might have been enabled, but its screenshot is missing.
   It neither supersedes DEC-101 nor establishes the deployed revision or
   publication path. If settings conflict with approved policy, resolve that
   discrepancy before proceeding.
2. Review the intended artifact and retain its revision-specific preview
   evidence, following [artifact preservation rules](operations.md#artifact-review).
3. Use the approved manual publication process. Receipt storage remains an
   unresolved choice; select it and retain production evidence so a later
   reader can establish what was published and how.

The previous automatic-publication guidance incorrectly treated the demonstration
as policy. Source: [demo note](../evidence/05-demo.txt). Supplied build and preview
evidence does not establish a production release; see [current status](status.md).

# Kestrel field catalogue context

Kestrel is a static catalogue of approved sample equipment manuals for a small
pilot team. Equipment specifications remain upstream. This record reconciles
the supplied September 1–25, 2026 evidence with the checked-in configuration;
no live environment was available for verification.

## Decisions and publication

- **DEC-101 — approved by owner Mira, September 8:** publication is manual,
  with optional CI, so the operator reviews every artifact. The recorded command
  is `wrangler pages deploy dist`. Automatic Git publication and mandatory CI
  are deferred proposals; revisit them if release frequency justifies setup.
  A later proposal date does not constitute approval.
  [Owner decision](evidence/02-owner.txt)
- The September 1 contributor design proposed publication on every main-branch
  push after mandatory CI, to reduce operator repetition and tie artifacts to
  source revisions. Its proposed 30-second timeout aimed to limit time occupied
  by failed builds. These were suggestions, not implementation or deployment
  evidence. DEC-101 settles publication policy; the current timeout is recorded
  below. [Original rationale](evidence/01-design.txt)
- **DEC-102 — approved by Mira, September 8:** only approved sample manuals may
  enter the catalogue. Public/customer uploads and external ingestion are not
  approved. Document rights and update ownership must be agreed before expanding
  sources. This boundary survives publication-process changes.
  [Owner decision](evidence/02-owner.txt)

## Verified configuration and supplied observations

The checked-in [service configuration](config/service.yaml) sets
`timeout_seconds: 45`, consistent with the September 25 operator update, which
records the change from 60 seconds. No production rollout or runtime observation
accompanies that change. [Operator update](evidence/07-update.txt)

The September 21 local build observation recorded the earlier 60-second setting,
a successful artifact build, and a staging-only preview
receipt naming revision `sample-17`. It does not establish production rollout,
the deployed revision, or the running pilot site's timeout. No production
receipt or runtime configuration export is supplied.
[Build observation](evidence/06-build.txt)

The September 20 demonstration note says Git integration **might** have been
enabled, but the screenshot is missing. Actual settings and the publication
path remain unverified, and no owner decision supersedes DEC-101. Confirm
settings before a real release and reconcile any automatic publication setting
with the approved manual policy; possible implementation is not approval.
Receipt storage has not been selected.
[Demonstration note](evidence/05-demo.txt)

Keep preview links with their artifact revision. A replacement produced by a
rebuild needs its own review; it does not inherit acceptance of the previous
preview. Keep the previous accepted artifact available until its replacement
is accepted, and do not reconstruct it from a newer revision and describe it as
the reviewed artifact. A failed preview alone does not establish a failed
production deployment. [September 13 reviewer guidance](evidence/03-review.txt)

its sparse-file flag when allocating the test volume, or quota estimates will
be wrong. Ask the storage maintainer before reserving the volume. Retain this
constraint for future exercises even after allocation or a successful restore.

and remains in place.

files.evidence/01-design.txt:
September 2, 2026 — Contributor draft design.
A hosted viewer could support shared review. A simple matcher might compare
item identifiers as numbers and treat blank quantities as zero. A batch of
100 rows was suggested for the first demonstration. These are unapproved
suggestions; they are not requirements or evidence of running behavior.
A discrepancy report should help a person investigate, not silently pick an
authoritative ledger. Export timestamps may explain differences between rows.
files.evidence/02-owner.txt:
September 7, 2026 — Owner Lina, DEC-201: approve offline CSV reports for the
pilot because operators work in a disconnected warehouse office. The tool
reads local exports and must not modify them. A hosted viewer remains an
unapproved proposal. Tool output does not approve corrections to warehouse
records or establish which ledger is financially authoritative.
DEC-202: match the pair item_id and location_id as opaque strings. Preserve
case and leading zeros; item-only or numeric matching can merge distinct
locations or records. A blank quantity means unknown, not zero. These
decisions supersede the corresponding September 2 draft suggestions.
files.evidence/03-usage.txt:
September 12, 2026 — Supported workflow note.
Run `oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv`. Inputs are
read-only and output must not overwrite either input. Keep source exports
until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report. The left export determines
field order, followed by right-only fields in their original order. Duplicate
item identifiers can represent separate locations; do not deduplicate them
automatically. Missing records may reflect filtered exports rather than deletion.
files.evidence/04-work.txt:
September 16, 2026 — Work list.
SAMPLE-201 is open: request an approved synthetic export containing one item
at two locations, then run the duplicate-location comparison. ENC-202 is
separately open: request an approved non-ASCII location sample from the
test maintainer. Passing the duplicate-location case cannot close ENC-202.
The person authorized to approve actual warehouse ledger corrections has
not been identified in the supplied records. Lina's tool-design role does
not establish that she has warehouse correction authority.
files.evidence/05-proposal.txt:
September 20, 2026 — Contributor viewer and JSON proposal.
A browser viewer might ease shared report review. JSON output could support
local downstream analysis without changing the offline boundary. Neither
proposal has owner approval in this note. The contributor made a local viewer
mockup; implementation of a demo does not establish an approved hosted service.
No delivery date, production rollout or telemetry system was approved.
files.evidence/06-check.txt:
September 21, 2026 — Repository and test observation.
The checked-in batch limit is 200 rows and CSV is the configured format.
A local unit test used a tiny synthetic input. That is not evidence of a
production installation, of representative warehouse coverage, or of an
accepted end-user report. No running installation's configuration is supplied.

# Matching details

## Approved matching semantics — DEC-202

Match the pair `item_id` and `location_id` as opaque strings, preserving case and leading zeros in both parts. Item-only or numeric matching can merge distinct locations or records. Duplicate item identifiers may represent separate locations and must not be automatically deduplicated. A blank quantity means unknown, not zero.

DEC-202 supersedes the numeric item matching and blank-as-zero suggestions in the September 2 draft. The September 22 review note reinforces this with the fixture example: item `"0042"` at location `"a"` is distinct from `"42"` at `"A"`.

## Interpretation limits

A discrepancy helps a person investigate; it does not silently select an authoritative ledger. Export timestamps may explain row differences. Missing records may reflect filtered exports rather than deletion. A blank quantity is missing evidence. Never rewrite source exports to make a comparison pass.

Sources: [draft design](../evidence/01-design.txt), [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [supported workflow](../evidence/03-usage.txt), and [uncommitted review note](../scratch/reviewer.txt).

See [operations](operations.md) for review handling and [working state](status.md) for outstanding coverage.

# Operator workflow

The supplied September 12 workflow documents:

```sh
oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv
```

Read local exports without modifying them. The output must not overwrite either input. Preserve source exports until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report; never rewrite inputs to make the comparison pass.

Preserve the left export's field order, then append right-only fields in their original order. Apply the [approved matching semantics](boundaries.md), including location in the key and preserving case and leading zeros.

The report supports human investigation. It neither approves warehouse ledger corrections nor establishes which ledger is financially authoritative. The person authorized to approve actual warehouse corrections remains unidentified. Lina's tool-design authority does not establish correction authority.

This is a documented workflow, not evidence that the command was run successfully in a live environment. No live environment access is supplied; installation and effective runtime configuration remain unverified.

Sources: [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [supported workflow](../evidence/03-usage.txt), [work list](../evidence/04-work.txt), [repository/test observation](../evidence/06-check.txt), and [review note](../scratch/reviewer.txt).

See [working state and next steps](status.md).

# Matching details

Owner Lina's September 7 **DEC-202** requires matching the pair `item_id` and `location_id` as opaque strings, preserving case and leading zeros. These decisions supersede the numeric matching and blank-as-zero suggestions in the unapproved September 2 draft. Sources: [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [draft rationale and suggestions](../evidence/01-design.txt).

The [September 22 uncommitted review note](../scratch/reviewer.txt) gives a concrete fixture distinction: item `"0042"` at location `"a"` is distinct from `"42"` at `"A"`. Preserve case and leading zeros in both parts of the key; a blank quantity is missing evidence.

Duplicate item identifiers can represent separate locations and must not be deduplicated automatically. Missing records may reflect filtered exports rather than deletion ([supported workflow](../evidence/03-usage.txt)). Export timestamps may help explain row differences; this remains a useful investigation consideration from the [draft](../evidence/01-design.txt), not evidence of implemented timestamp handling.

# Boundaries and matching

Owner Lina approved these rules on September 7, 2026:

- **DEC-201:** read local exports and produce offline CSV reports for the pilot. Inputs must not be modified. A discrepancy report supports human investigation; it neither authorizes warehouse corrections nor establishes which ledger is financially authoritative.
- **DEC-202:** match the pair `item_id` and `location_id` as opaque strings, preserving case and leading zeros in both parts. Item-only or numeric matching can merge distinct locations or records. Blank quantity means unknown, not zero.

These decisions supersede the September 2 contributor draft's numeric item-only matching and blank-to-zero suggestions. The earlier claim here that the report authorizes source corrections was unsupported.

The September 22 uncommitted review note reinforces these rules: item `"0042"` at location `"a"` is distinct from `"42"` at `"A"`. Preserve the source exports during discrepancy review; never rewrite them to make a comparison pass. A blank quantity is missing evidence.

Sources: [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [draft design](../evidence/01-design.txt), [review note](../scratch/reviewer.txt). See [operations](operations.md) for workflow and [status](status.md) for the unresolved correction authority.
files.notes/operations.md:
# Operations and rationale

The September 7 owner decision chose offline CSV for operators in a disconnected warehouse office. Opaque composite identifiers prevent accidental record merging; see [matching rules](boundaries.md).

The September 12 supported workflow is:

```sh
oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv
```

Inputs are read-only, and the output must not overwrite either input. Retain source exports until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report. Preserve the left export's field order, then append right-only fields in their original order.

Duplicate item identifiers may represent separate locations; do not deduplicate them automatically. Missing records may reflect filtered exports rather than deletion. Export timestamps may explain row differences. The report helps a person investigate; it does not select an authoritative ledger or approve corrections.

This is a documented workflow, not a claim that it was executed or verified in a live environment during this handoff.

Sources: [owner decisions](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [supported workflow](../evidence/03-usage.txt), [draft's investigation rationale](../evidence/01-design.txt).
files.notes/release.md:
# Output scope and proposals

Offline CSV reports are approved for the pilot under DEC-201 (September 7). CSV is also the currently configured format in [report.yaml](../config/report.yaml). This does not establish that CSV is the only format the project will ever support.

The September 20 contributor proposal suggests a browser viewer for shared review and JSON for local downstream analysis. Neither has owner approval in the supplied evidence. JSON could fit the offline boundary, but remains a proposal. A local viewer mockup is implementation evidence for a demo, not approval of a hosted service. The hosted viewer suggested in the September 2 draft remains unapproved; the newer proposal does not supersede DEC-201.

No delivery date, production rollout, or telemetry system was approved in the supplied proposal. Future output or hosting changes need an explicit scope decision; they are not current commitments.

Sources: [draft](../evidence/01-design.txt), [owner decision](../evidence/02-owner.txt), [viewer and JSON proposal](../evidence/05-proposal.txt), [repository observation](../evidence/06-check.txt).

# Oriole warehouse reconciliation

An offline tool that compares local warehouse exports for human review without modifying either input.

Raw project/work evidence is in `evidence/`, configuration in `config/`, and uncommitted work notes in `scratch/`.

## Continuing the work

This README is the maintained handoff, reconciled from the supplied records through September 22, 2026. It describes approved intent, the documented workflow, and the limits of the available evidence; no live installation was supplied or verified. Keep the linked source records for their original context.

## Approved scope and decisions

- **DEC-201 — offline CSV pilot:** Owner Lina approved local, read-only export comparison because operators work in a disconnected warehouse office. Inputs must not be modified. Reports support human investigation; they neither authorize warehouse corrections nor establish which ledger is financially authoritative.
- **DEC-202 — matching and unknown quantities:** Match the pair `item_id` and `location_id` as opaque strings, preserving case and leading zeros in both. Item-only or numeric matching can merge distinct records or locations. A blank quantity means unknown, not zero.

These [September 7 owner decisions](evidence/02-owner.txt) supersede the numeric matching and blank-as-zero suggestions in the [September 2 draft](evidence/01-design.txt). The draft's hosted viewer and 100-row demonstration batch were unapproved suggestions, not requirements or observed behavior. Its useful investigation context remains: export timestamps may explain row differences, and a report should not silently select an authoritative ledger.

The [September 22 review note](scratch/reviewer.txt) reinforces DEC-202: item `"0042"` at location `"a"` is distinct from item `"42"` at location `"A"`. Preserve this fixture distinction. Blank quantities are missing evidence; never rewrite exports to make a comparison pass.

## Documented workflow

The [supported workflow note](evidence/03-usage.txt) gives:

```sh
oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv
```

- Read inputs without modifying them, and do not let output overwrite either input.
- Retain source exports until a reviewer accepts or rejects the report.
- Use the left export's field order, then append right-only fields in their original order.
- Do not automatically deduplicate repeated item identifiers: they can represent separate locations.
- Investigate missing records; filtered exports may explain them, so absence does not establish deletion.

This is a documented command, not a command verified against a running installation in this handoff.

## Configuration and evidence limits

[config/report.yaml](config/report.yaml) sets `batch_rows: 200` and `formats: [csv]`, consistent with the [September 21 observation](evidence/06-check.txt). Use 200 when describing the checked-in batch limit; the earlier 100-row suggestion is not the current configuration. No running installation's configuration is supplied.

The September 21 note reports a local unit test using a tiny synthetic input. That does not establish representative warehouse coverage, production installation, or acceptance of an end-user report. It also does not close the sample requests below.

## Proposals and unresolved work

The [September 20 proposal](evidence/05-proposal.txt) suggests a browser viewer for shared review and JSON output for local downstream analysis. Neither has owner approval. JSON could preserve the offline boundary, but CSV remains the configured format. A local viewer mockup is reported; it does not establish approval for a hosted service. No delivery date, production rollout, or telemetry system was approved.

The [September 16 work list](evidence/04-work.txt) leaves these items open:

| Item | Next action and constraint |
| --- | --- |
| SAMPLE-201 | Request an approved synthetic export with one item at two locations, then run the duplicate-location comparison. No completion evidence is supplied. |
| ENC-202 | Separately request an approved non-ASCII location sample from the test maintainer. Passing the duplicate-location case cannot close this item. |
| Warehouse correction authority | Identify who is authorized to approve actual ledger corrections. The supplied records do not name that person; Lina's tool-design authority does not establish correction authority. |

Continue from these open items using approved samples. Record subsequent decisions and verification evidence here with source references, retaining the distinction between proposals, approved requirements, repository settings, and observed behavior.

# Oriole warehouse reconciliation

An offline tool that compares local warehouse exports for human review without modifying either input.

Start with [project context](context.md) for approved decisions, the supported workflow, evidence limits, and unresolved work.

Raw project/work evidence is in `evidence/`, configuration in `config/`, and uncommitted work notes in `scratch/`.
files.context.md:
# Oriole project context

Oriole compares local warehouse exports to produce discrepancy reports for human
investigation. This record reconciles the supplied evidence through September 25,
2026 with the repository configuration reviewed on September 27, 2026.

## Approved decisions and constraints

Owner Lina approved these tool-design decisions on September 7 in the
[owner record](evidence/02-owner.txt):

- **DEC-201:** the pilot produces offline CSV reports because operators work in a
  disconnected warehouse office. Inputs remain read-only. Reports neither approve
  warehouse corrections nor establish which ledger is financially authoritative.
- **DEC-202:** match the pair `item_id` and `location_id` as opaque strings,
  preserving case and leading zeros. Numeric or item-only matching can merge
  distinct records or locations. Blank quantities mean unknown, not zero.

These supersede the numeric matching and blank-as-zero suggestions in the
[September 2 contributor draft](evidence/01-design.txt). Its hosted viewer and
100-row demonstration batch were unapproved suggestions, not requirements or
observed behavior. Its useful rationale remains: reports help people investigate,
and export timestamps may explain row differences.

In the [September 25 owner and test maintainer update](evidence/07-update.txt),
Lina approved **DEC-203:** optional local JSON reports alongside CSV for downstream
offline analysis. This supersedes CSV-only output under DEC-201; the offline and
read-only boundaries remain in force. DEC-202 matching and blank-quantity
semantics remain unchanged. The hosted viewer remains unapproved.

The [uncommitted September 22 review note](scratch/reviewer.txt) reinforces the
matching rule with a concrete fixture: item `"0042"` at location `"a"` is distinct
from `"42"` at `"A"`. Preserve that note; it also cautions against rewriting
exports to make a comparison pass and treats blank quantities as missing evidence.

## Repository state and verification limits

[Configuration](config/report.yaml) sets `batch_rows: 125` and `formats: [csv, json]`,
consistent with the [September 25 update](evidence/07-update.txt). The 125-row
value is a repository fact, not evidence of separate owner approval or a running
installation's settings.

The [September 21 observation](evidence/06-check.txt) recorded the earlier
200-row, CSV-only configuration and a local unit test using tiny synthetic input.
The September 25 update closes **SAMPLE-201**: its synthetic fixture containing
one item at two locations was created and the comparison passed, test **D201**. These tests do not
establish representative warehouse coverage, an accepted end-user report, or a
production installation. No live access or running installation configuration
is supplied, and the update reports no running installation observed. The available
files do not include implementation code to verify
matching or workflow behavior; the requirements below come from the supplied
decision and workflow records.

## Supported workflow

The [September 12 workflow note](evidence/03-usage.txt) specifies:

```sh
oriole compare left.csv right.csv --output report.csv
```

- Output must not overwrite either input. Keep both source exports until a
  reviewer accepts or rejects the report.
- The left export determines field order, followed by right-only fields in their
  original order.
- Do not automatically deduplicate item identifiers: repeated items can represent
  separate locations. Missing records may reflect filtered exports rather than
  deletion.

This is the documented command, not a command executed during this documentation
review.

## Unresolved work and proposals

The following items from the [September 16 work list](evidence/04-work.txt) remain
open in the [September 25 update](evidence/07-update.txt):

| Item | Next action or required clarification |
| --- | --- |
| ENC-202 | Request an approved non-ASCII location sample from the test maintainer. Passing the duplicate-location case cannot close this item. |
| Warehouse correction authority | Identify who can approve actual ledger corrections before treating a report as authorization. Lina's tool-design role does not establish that authority. |

The browser viewer for shared review in the
[September 20 proposal](evidence/05-proposal.txt) remains unapproved. Its local
JSON output proposal is now approved under DEC-203 above. A contributor's local
viewer mockup does not establish an approved hosted service. Viewer adoption
needs an owner decision; no delivery date, production rollout, or telemetry system
was approved.
